v1_human_g3_constraints.c_1: the request cannot exceed the resource inventory

v1_human_g3_frs.fr_1: The input for resources must be a dictionary
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_2: For requests, must be a list where each element is a dictionary
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_3: Every resource requested must exist in resources
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_4: The amount requested must not be negative
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_6: The amount must be an integer

v1_human_g3_goal: Determines whether a list of resource requests can be satisfied given limited capacity. For example, if one is assigned at 10, the system checks if the request is greater than 10.
v1_human_g3_input:
Input 1 is a dictionary that contains the name of the resource and its associated minimum capacity. Ex. resources: {'cpu': 10}

Input 2 is the requests for resource allocation. It is a list which contains dictionaries. Each dictionary is a request for the associated resource. Ex. [{'cpu': 2}, {'mem': 8}, {'cpu': 3}, {'mem': 10}]

v1_human_g3_invariants.inv_1: resource amount must not exceed available capacity
v1_human_g3_invariants.inv_2: all resource requests must be positive
v1_human_g3_invariants.inv_3: every resource requested must exist in resources

v1_human_g3_neg_req.neg_req_1: The system must not allocate resources above available capacity
v1_human_g3_neg_req.neg_req_2: The system must not request for resources that have not been declared

v1_human_g3_output: The function returns a boolean value (true or false) which indicates if the request has been fulfilled.
